decisions.summary: One command `make record` (assemble / CHECK=1 / PAGE= / SPLIT=), and the citations page assembled in TWO PASSES so `citations.py` keeps reading an assembled page
decisions.why: Round 1's D-citations-reader finding is RESOLVED. The plan's source-code table now marks citations.py UNCHANGED as a reader, T16 says the same, and the second Complexity Tracking entry is dissolved rather than justified - which is what FR-029 asks for. Two mechanical caveats the implementation must close, neither a fidelity departure: (a) `citations.derive(page_rel)` reads the page from DISK, so `hand THAT page to the derivation` means writing the first-pass page before calling it; (b) `with_works()` RAISES unless the page carries WORKS_OPEN and WORKS_CLOSE, and both marker comments are emitted by `works_html()` (program bytes today), so an `empty works region` must still carry the two markers - taken from citations.py's constants, not retyped - and the contract's new sentence `No page bytes live in the program` needs to say `no hand-authored page bytes`.

decisions.summary: A page is a directory of fragments: _front, NNN-<slug>, _tail, prefixes gapped by ten, three digits a question and four a registry entry
decisions.why: FR-011 and FR-012 state exactly this, including the gap and the digit counts. Unchanged from round 1.

decisions.summary: The registry is a page whose works-cited section carries its 920 entries in a subdirectory, with attested-instances and setting-canon as siblings
decisions.why: FR-007 and FR-009, verified against SOURCES.html in round 1. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: The citing rules and the re-sourcing queue ride inside _front.html as part of the commented-out block rather than each becoming its own file
decisions.why: Unchanged from round 1: measured, both offsets fall inside ONE 8,042-byte HTML comment, so FR-008's premise that they are live sections is factually wrong, and its stated purpose - no prose of the registry living only inside a program - is met in full.

decisions.summary: _citations-front runs through `<section class="works">` and its `<h2 id="works-cited">`; a new _citations-mid holds `</section>`, `<h2 id="notes">` and `<section class="footnotes"><ol>`
decisions.why:
RESOLVED. Re-measured on all 19 citations pages: the bytes before the derived block are `

The works cited on this page

`, identical on all 19, and the bytes after WORKS_CLOSE are `

The notes

    `, identical on all 19. Both now belong to a fragment, so no hand-authored byte is dropped or retyped in the program. One leftover the fix missed: contracts/fragment-format.md's `What each fragment must contain` table still carries a row for `_citations-works.html`, the fragment D1 abolished, and carries no row for `_citations-mid.html` or `_citations-tail.html`.

decisions.summary: A research page is cut on `<h2>` alone; the closing run is the tail and a page that does not end that way is refused; the `fn-<n>` refusal applies from stage 3 on
decisions.why: RESOLVED on all three of round 1's boundaries, and each stated premise re-measured here. (a) All 39 files of the record (19 research pages, 19 citations pages, SOURCES.html) end `</main></body></html>`, so data-model.md's `every one of the record's 38 pages ends in exactly that` holds and the tail is defined rather than guessed. (b) Exactly 14 `<h3>` stand outside comments in research pages, on the six pages named (capitals 2, government 3, sizing 1, fields 5, homesteads 2, urban-features 1); the cut-on-`<h2>`-alone rule keeps them inside their question, and FR-023 now says a check pointed at one reads the question that contains it. (c) The `fn-<n>`/`fnref-<n>` refusal is staged to stage 3 in both the rules table and the refusals table, so it no longer forbids what a byte-identical stage-2 fragment must carry.

decisions.summary: The constitution XIII baseline is a detached-worktree `make done`, recorded as m:baseline-done
decisions.why: RESOLVED. T01 and the plan's XIII clause both name `make done` and state the reason a quick-only baseline cannot serve (it cannot tell a new coverage-floor or tests/full failure from an old one). The run is reported in flight. Owed when it lands: measurements.json still holds only `baseline-quick`, whose note calls itself `Constitution XIII baseline for feature 258`; that note must be corrected or the entry retired when `baseline-done` is recorded, or the record carries two claims to the same title.

decisions.summary: Stage 3 MOVES the notes on the 16 pages whose references are not ascending; the invariant held and tested is the assertion-to-note PAIRING plus the unchanged multiset of note bodies per page
decisions.why: RESOLVED as a declaration. The reorder is entailed by the structure the GM approved (the notes split by the SAME section as the prose, siblings of their question) plus the renumbering he brought into scope, so it is not a narrowing; what round 1 found wrong was that it was undeclared and that the declared test - strip the numbers and require equality - could not pass. It is now declared in the plan's stage table, D4a, the contract's invariant section, spec SC-003, US4 scenario 1, and T17/T18, and the test is order-aware.

decisions.summary: Stage 3's reader-visible diff is declared complete at the numbers and the note order - `nothing else differs` (plan D4a, spec SC-003, contracts/fragment-format.md's round-trip section)
decisions.why: MEASURED, and false: the WORKS SECTION reorders too, on exactly the same 16 pages. `citations.cited_keys()` lists the works `in order of first citation` by walking the notes in their order on the citations page, so D1's second pass derives the works block from the REORDERED page. Simulating stage 3 over the real record - notes taken in the research page's reference order, then `cited_keys` re-derived - changes the works key order on 16 of 19 pages (ways: nrcs-ts14q-abutments first instead of ritter-timber-bridges; capitals, fields, water and 12 others likewise; the key SET is unchanged on every page). The works section is 16 to 231 `<h3>` blocks a reader sees at the top of the page, so this is a third reader-visible change, and it is the one the GM's approved point 3 was about (`the diff proves the split changed nothing a reader sees`) - the renumbering is the carve-out he granted, this one nobody has stated or put to him. Concretely it breaks the plan's own acceptance: SC-003's `nothing else differs` and the contract's `with the numbers and the note order set aside, nothing else differs` would FAIL on 16 pages at T18. The plan must either (i) declare the works reorder as a third consequence in D4a, SC-003 and the contract's invariant list, and hold the works key SET rather than its order, or (ii) preserve the works order by deriving `cited_keys` from something the renumbering does not move; the choice is the plan's, the silence is not.

decisions.summary: No index file: a source is found by a glob on its key, a question by a grep over its page directory
decisions.why: The GM left the index open and accepted the session's answer that there be none; the spec records it in Assumptions and FR-010. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Note keys derived by the splitter from the leading source key, an ordinal for a repeat, the question slug plus ordinal for the 326 notes that lead with none
decisions.why: FR-017 and R5. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Numbers allocated at assembly in document order; each reference gets a document-unique id; the 4 missing ids and the 2 duplicated ones fall out fixed
decisions.why: FR-019, FR-021, FR-022 and constitution XIV; the GM brought the renumbering in with `do that as part of it`. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: The staleness check runs both at the gate and at the push, because a record-only delta takes the DIRECT route
decisions.why: FR-003 and FR-004 name both places for that stated reason; it enforces the requested behavior and nothing else. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: record-edit-hooks.sh rewrites an Edit aimed at an assembled page to the one fragment holding its old_string, refuses where none or several do, and always refuses a Write
decisions.why: FR-028 word for word, and its reach is the record's assembled pages only. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: The three prepass scripts learn to address one question and the four agent contracts are rewritten to read the fragment
decisions.why: FR-023 and FR-024, with feature 256's omitClaudeMd as the stated reason the rule must live in the contracts. FR-023 now also settles the `<h3>` case. Unchanged otherwise.

decisions.summary: The splitter is kept in the tree after its one-time use, to hold assemble(split(page)) == page over the real record
decisions.why: The justification is real and the cost (the 100% floor) is named rather than waived. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: The performance bookends are N/A and the gate's cost is measured instead (R7, T02 and T27)
decisions.why: Honest: no generator, no .gen.py and no map-drawing code is touched; what this feature can slow is the gate, and the plan measures it at both ends. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Constitution XII is N/A because every assertion keeps its text, its footnote and its evidence class
decisions.why: Honest on the evidence: no claim about the world is added, removed or re-grounded. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Three stages, each landing on its own, the renumbering last
decisions.why: The spec's Assumptions state exactly this, and stages 1 and 2 are proven by an empty diff at their own landing commits. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: R1's figures, re-run rather than read
decisions.why: `python3 specs/258-.../measure.py R1` re-ran here and reproduces every figure the plan and spec quote, including the largest single question, 37,583 bytes (fields.html). An independent comment-aware cut over all 19 research pages agrees: fields.html 37,583, then urban-features 24,322 (measure.py's 24,346 differs only by where the tail is cut). Round 1's `largest is 24,346` was wrong - it was urban-features' own maximum, not the record's - and R1 and SC-001 are right. SC-001's 40,000-byte bar therefore STANDS, clearing the largest question by 2,417 bytes; the spec already says it clears `with little to spare - deliberately`, so the bar is stated honestly and needs no change.
